rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview and Goal 2 Gameplay Overview 3 End of Round 4 End of Game 5 Scoring Overview and Goal Popcorn is a bag-building game for 2 to 4 players. You each manage a movie theater and want to show the best movies to satisfy Guests, and also gain as much Popcorn as possible. The game plays over around 9 rounds, each with 3 phases. In turn order, you may buy a movie, build a theater, and attract new Guests. Then, simultaneously, welcome your customers and seat them in your theaters. Optimize their seats to take the best actions, which will let you improve your cinema, influence your Guests, grow your audience, and gain money and Popcorn. You begin the game with a movie, a bag with 5 white guests, 1 guest of each other colour, and an additional guest matching your start movie's colour. 1 guest of each other colour also begin on your exit space. A total of 14 guests. At the end of the last round, the player with the most Popcorn wins the game! Gameplay Overview A round plays over 3 phases: Buying and Advertising, Showings, then End of Round. Play begins with the player with the First Player marker, then continues clockwise. Phase 1: Buying and Advertising In this phase, each player takes a turn. On your turn, you may take these actions in any order (all these actions are optional): Buy a movie (Maximum 1 time per turn): Immediately place the movie on one of your theatres, sending the previous movie to your archive. If you place the movie in a matching theatre (1, 2, or 3 seats) you will immediately gain the bonus shown. Movies from the Top Row cost an extra $2 to purchase, you immediately gain a guest of the matching color from the reserve (or an Exit Zone) exactly like using Advertising tokens. Buy a theater (Maximum 1 time per turn) Note: You cannot take this action on your first turn. Activate Advertising tokens: Take one guest of the matching color from the reserve, and put it directly in your bag. If there are no guests of that color in the reserve, you may instead take one from any player's Exit Zone. If it's a "White in Bag" advertising token, you instead place a white guest from the reserve into any opponent bag. Alternately, you can simply take the token back to your supply worth no effect. Tokens can be left on the board from turn to turn, if you do not want the effect of them immediately. Note that you only have 3 Advertising tokens. If all of them are already in play, you ignore any actions that would let you play more advertising tokens. Phase 2: Showings Open Cinema Draw as many Guests from your bag as the number shown by the cube on your audience track at the bottom of your Cinema board Place Guests After drawing your Guests, place them in your theaters as follows: You may only place Guests in theaters that are showing a movie. In each theater, place Guests in seat order (#1, then #2, etc.). You do not have to fill a theater before seating Guests in a different one. If you draw more Guests than there are available seats in your theaters showing a movie, place the extra Guests in the exit zone of your cinema. Note: You may place a Guest on a seat of any color, but it’s better to place them on gray seats or those of their color, and also in theaters with movies of their color. Once all Guests are placed, continue to Seat and Movie Actions. Phase 3: Seat and Movie Actions Now is when you may activate your Guests. Move from theater to theater, in any order you choose. You must activate all Guests in a single theater, in ascending order of their seats, before moving to any other theater. When you activate a Guest, they do the following in order: 1. Take 1 Seat action, if possible. 2. Take 1 Movie action, if possible. 3. Move to the exit. Note: You are never required to take an action. End of Round Theatrical Run Move your Lobby sliders 1 space up on each of your Movie cards, covering 1 more action in each of your theaters. These actions will no longer be available in future rounds. You may continue showing a movie in your cinema even if it no longer has available actions. You may still place Guests in its theater to take Seat actions. End of Game The final round is the round in which the Final Showing card is revealed in the Movies deck. Position in Deck 2 players = 10 cards below it 3&4 players = 5 cards below it Scoring Popcorn you gained during the game. 1 Popcorn for every $5 you have. The player(s) with the highest total costing 3 theaters gain(s) the first Theater trophy (5 Popcorn with 3 or 4 players, 3 Popcorn with 2 players). With 3 or 4 players, if there is not a tie for first place, the second highest gains the second Theater trophy (3 Popcorn). Gain the corresponding Popcorn from Award cards. You can treat remaining Advertising tokens toward Award cards! The color of the 5 color advertising needs to be chosen. The "White to bag" can be used to remove one of your white guests. In case of a tie between 2 or more players, the one with the fewest archived movies wins. If there is still a tie, tied players share the victory.

---

In Popcorn, each player manages their own movie theater and tries to show the best combination of movies in order to attract guests to their seats.

The game plays out over nine rounds, and in each round you may acquire a new movie, build or upgrade your theater, and use advertising to attract new guests — then it's showtime, with you drawing guests at random from your bag to see who has shown up. Place guests in the right seats to activate special powers; match them with the right movies, and you get a movie bonus as well, thanks to their enthusiasm for your good taste.

After watching films in your theater, guests might be spirited away to other theaters thanks to ads presented by those theater owners - but you'll probably do the same to them, too.

The bonuses from a movie get worse the longer it runs, so be sure to bring in fresh films to keep guests on the edge of your seats. After all, happy guests can help your theater win awards in town; more importantly, they can keep the "popcorn" piling up in your coffers, and whichever theater owner fills their popcorn box the best wins.
community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Many small, fiddly components, tons of rules to explain, some interaction but mostly the focus is on one's own gameboard. Not my type of game.

[Rating: 3/10] The best idea in Popcorn is the theme.  There's almost no game here, just board maintenance and tons of rules to follow.  Inelegant.  Simply reading the stack of movies one-by-one, is tons more fun than playing this.

[Rating: 3/10] The fact there is no wild meeple makes me gives this a bad rating. A bag builder needs a wild especially as you pull 3-4 meeples early and mid game.

[Rating: 4/10] A lot luck between movie cards, theater tiles, goal cards, and the guests you draw. Money is also very tight if you do not exclusively lean into heavy money early. If you run out of money with no way to gain more, you are out of the game.   Also, the goal cards are definitely not balanced and some are very dependent on luck. A waste goal draw is pretty devastating on points.

[Rating: 4/10] [ImageID=8623640small] JASE.   [b]Pros:[/b] The economy is well-balanced, you usually can't get everything you want and have to compromise.   I like the closed economy of meeples, where you get to take meeples from other players if there's none in the neutral market.  I like the production, the artwork is inviting and the setting is well realized even if it's not very thematic.  [b]Cons:[/b] For being a bag builder it has no arc. You get the same things every round, you just get more of it later in the game. You get some new meeples, you get rid of some meeples, but in the end it doesn't reall

[Rating: 4/10] There was so much potential for this theme but they absolutely floundered it. I think they should have leaned more into realistic theatre things (ex: 100 seats in a theatre, filing certain # of them based on [whatever], leaning more into the sales/demand aspect of movies in theatres, etc.) but instead it's extremely surface level and it doesn't work out very well. So not only was the theme not fully realized, but what they came up with wasn't very fun either. Was waiting for the game to be over. Part of this may be due to first-time-play, but the failure of taking advantage of this cool concep

[Rating: 5/10] I think I wanted this game to be less luck dependent and have time for one's bag to develop...but players really are at the mercy of what theaters come out and what seats are available...and the later you go in turn order the less choice you have.  I'm also not overly fond of the guest stealing mechanic although I reckon one could say it's somewhat thematic and you're taking patrons away from a rival theater...it's just one more thing beyond your control.
